decisions.reason: Across the five experiments re-testing Longoni et al. (1993), the authors report a combination of replicated and non-replicated findings: the phonemic similarity effect replicated across experiments (including preservation across a 10-second delay in Experiment 5), and the irrelevant speech main effect and lack of interaction with word length replicated in Experiment 3, whereas the articulatory suppression effect, the word length main effect in Experiment 3, the presentation speed effect in Experiment 4, the recall delay main effect in Experiment 5, and additivity between word length and phonemic similarity in Experiment 2 did not replicate. Although methodological limitations are discussed, the authors do not declare their study uninformative, confirming a 'mixed' outcome.
